title: Pullback composition and inverse identities commute with integral scalar extension
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$ and finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. For a scheme $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties] and $F\in\{E,L\}$ let $D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_F)$ be the derived-complete integral constructible category [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], and let $T_W:D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)\to D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_L)$, $K\mapsto K\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}\mathcal O_L$, be integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension]. For a morphism $f:W'\to W$ of such schemes let $Lf_F^*$ be the integral derived pullback over $\mathcal O_F$ [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and let $\alpha^f_K:T_{W'}(Lf_E^*K)\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf_L^*(T_WK)$, for $K\in D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$, be the natural scalar-extension comparison of [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension].

Throughout, use the canonical comparison families specified by the whole-system realization of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization], not arbitrary natural isomorphisms between the same functors.

1. *Composition.* Let $h:Z\to W$ and $k:W\to V$ be morphisms of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible, and let $c^{\mathcal O_F}_{h,k}:L(k\circ h)_F^*\xrightarrow{\sim}Lh_F^*Lk_F^*$ be the integral composition isomorphisms of [lem-pod-integral-pullback-composition]. Then for every $K\in D^b_c(V,\mathcal O_E)$
$$Lh_L^*(\alpha^k_K)\circ\alpha^h_{Lk_E^*K}\circ T_Z\bigl(c^{\mathcal O_E}_{h,k}(K)\bigr)=c^{\mathcal O_L}_{h,k}(T_VK)\circ\alpha^{k\circ h}_K$$
as isomorphisms $T_Z(L(k\circ h)_E^*K)\to Lh_L^*Lk_L^*(T_VK)$.

2. *Inverse identities along an isomorphism.* Let $g:X\to Y$ be an isomorphism of schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible, with inverse $\bar g:Y\to X$, and write $g^{-1},\bar g^{-1}$ for the inverse-image functors on pro-etale module sheaves [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For $F\in\{E,L\}$ and $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_F)$ let $\lambda^g_K:Lg_F^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}g^{-1}K$ and $\lambda^{\bar g}$ be the canonical isomorphisms of [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback], normalized as $(\kappa^{g,F}_K)^{-1}$ and $(\kappa^{\bar g,F})^{-1}$, respectively, where $\kappa$ is the specified quotient-cone map of [def-weil-inverse-image-pullback-comparison](b), invertible on derived-complete objects by [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-comparison-normalization]. Let
$$\epsilon^F_K:L\bar g_F^*Lg_F^*K\xrightarrow{\ \lambda^{\bar g}_{Lg_F^*K}\ }\bar g^{-1}Lg_F^*K\xrightarrow{\ \bar g^{-1}(\lambda^g_K)\ }\bar g^{-1}g^{-1}K\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }K,$$
the last arrow being the canonical isomorphism of inverse images along $g\circ\bar g=\mathrm{id}_Y$ [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image]. Then for every $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$
$$\epsilon^L_{T_YK}\circ L\bar g_L^*(\alpha^g_K)\circ\alpha^{\bar g}_{Lg_E^*K}=T_Y(\epsilon^E_K)$$
as isomorphisms $T_Y(L\bar g_E^*Lg_E^*K)\to T_YK$.

Naturality of the adjunction counit gives their exact mate equations (composition_reduction and scalar_reduction). The actual unit is invertible on the constructible target by D.coefficient.complete, so equality after simultaneous reduction reflects equality of ambient derived arrows. Postcompose by the invertible iterated pullback/scalar counits. Their naturality and the derived_mixed equation of integralQuotientMixedCoherence identify the two resulting entire-system maps. Cancel the counits and reflect equality through reduction, proving clause (1) for this D, without choosing a different coherent system.

Move inverse image of lambda past beta_inv by beta_naturality. Identify the normalized derived counits by uniqueness from Step 1 and substitute the second equation of completedInverseImage_scalarCounit. Functoriality of scalar extension combines the resulting factors to scalar extension of epsilon_E, proving clause (2). These are identities of entire ambient derived arrows, with no finite-reduction detection or Tor-amplitude bound.
